steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Conceptual fly-over:

1. Break text into tokens.  
2. Turn each token into a vector (embedding) and add a “where it is” vector (positional encoding).  
3. Pass the sequence through many identical layers.  Each layer does:

   a. Self-Attention  
      • For every token, compute three projections: Query, Key, Value.  
      • Compare the Query of one token with the Keys of all tokens to get attention weights (How much should this word look at every other word?).  
      • Form a weighted sum of the Value vectors—this is what the token “knows” after looking around.  
      • Do this in several “heads” (multi-head attention) so the model can focus on multiple relational patterns at once.

   b. Add & Layer-Norm (keeps information from the previous step and stabilizes training).

   c. Feed-Forward Network  
      • Two simple fully connected layers applied to each token separately, adding non-linearity and mixing features.

   d. Another Add & Layer-Norm.

4. Stack of these layers lets tokens repeatedly refine what they know about the whole sequence, building rich contextual representations.

5. In encoder-only models (e.g., BERT) the final token vectors feed a task-specific head.  
   In encoder-decoder models (e.g., original Transformer) a decoder with masked self-attention generates output tokens step by step, consulting the encoder’s representations.  
   In decoder-only models (e.g., GPT) the same masked self-attention predicts the next token directly.

Key idea: Everything is driven by attention, not recurrence or convolutions, letting the model see and relate all tokens in parallel while scaling efficiently on modern hardware.
